title: The president of the United States signs controversial vaccine policy order

The order recommends separating the MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) vaccine into three separate shots administered in separate medical visits rather than as a combined vaccination. The order directs the nation's health agencies and advises states to revise their vaccine administration rules. The order also calls for reducing the number of childhood vaccines administered overall and for narrowing which vaccines are included in childhood immunization schedules. The president and HHS Secretary RFK Jr. referenced autism during the signing, despite scientific studies showing no link between vaccines and autism. The Trump administration had previously avoided public discussions of vaccine policy due to political concerns but changed course with this order. title: Major European rivers reach record low water levels in July
summary: Major European rivers—the Rhine, Rhone, and Danube—reached record low water levels in July 2026, marking the lowest flows recorded during that month since records began. The drought, driven by a series of heat waves, created a drought corridor stretching from the Rhine delta to the lower Danube across April to July 2026. River flows dropped to their lowest levels in seven years. Hydropower generation across the corridor fell approximately one-fifth below recent norms, with the worst-hit systems experiencing drops of one-third to one-half. Nuclear plants along the Danube also reduced output as cooling water became scarce. Gas imports and unusually wet conditions in Iberia helped offset energy shortfalls, though at rising prices. The low water levels disrupted river cruises and stranded houseboats, affecting the region's heavy industries that depend on these vital waterways for transport and cooling.

title: OpenAI pauses Astra development over cybersecurity concerns
summary: OpenAI announced on August 7, 2026 that it is pausing some development activities for its upcoming AI model Astra after internal cybersecurity evaluations determined the model has reached or cannot be ruled out as having "critical" cybersecurity capabilities. The evaluations revealed that Astra demonstrated significant advances in autonomous coding and the ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities without human intervention, potentially including autonomous cyberattack capabilities. The model can independently attack defended systems. This designation as reaching the "critical cybersecurity threshold" prompted OpenAI to implement tighter controls and strengthen safeguards. The current GPT-5.6-Sol model is assigned only a "high" cybersecurity threshold, while Astra represents a step above that. OpenAI stated it cannot rule out that Astra possesses these critical cyber capabilities, which triggered the company to slow the model's release and pause certain work to implement enhanced security measures before proceeding further.

summary: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity initiative with GPT-5.6-Cyber, a specialized model for authorized vulnerability research that achieves 95% task completion with reduced refusals, while establishing partnerships with 16 major organizations to counter autonomous AI-driven cyber threats.

title: Multistate water system attacks suspected to be Iran-linked
summary: Cyberattacks on U.S. water systems have affected at least a dozen states, with attackers suspected to be linked to Iran. New Jersey and Alabama were among the states that confirmed their water facilities targeted. The campaign involved compromised industrial control systems (ICS) at water and wastewater utilities that were poorly secured and internet-exposed. The attacks targeted programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and other operational technology infrastructure. This represents what appears to be the broadest known coordinated cyber campaign against U.S. municipal water systems. The FBI and federal officials confirmed involvement of Iran-backed threat actors in the incidents.

title: 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes Colombia, killing at least 111
summary: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, August 10, 2026, killing at least 111 people. The epicenter was located in San José del Palmar, approximately 250 miles west of Colombia's capital Bogotá. The tremor was felt across the region, including in Bogotá, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela. The earthquake occurred along the Pacific Ring of Fire and struck shortly after 7:30 a.m. local time. Emergency teams were conducting search and rescue operations in collapsed buildings. The earthquake was described as the strongest to hit the region in recent years, causing widespread destruction across western Colombia.

title: Ukraine reports up to 50,000 North Korean troops deploying to Russia
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia plans to deploy up to 50,000 North Korean troops to fight in the ongoing war against Ukraine. According to reports from August 9-10, 2026, Zelenskyy indicated the deployment could range from 30,000 to 50,000 North Korean soldiers. He characterized the deployment as part of Russia's strategy to involve North Korean forces in combat operations and gain military experience. The announcement came amid reports that Russia had received additional ballistic missiles from North Korea. Zelenskyy called for support from South Korea and other allies, including air defense systems, in response to the North Korean military involvement and ongoing Russian missile strikes against Ukrainian targets.

title: Ukraine launches deadly drone strike on Russian oil hub, killing 13
summary: Ukrainian forces conducted a drone strike on the Nizhnekamsk oil hub in Russia's Tatarstan region, killing at least 13 people and wounding 75, marking one of the deadliest Ukrainian attacks in two years as part of a campaign to damage Russian fuel supplies.
